title: LIVE LIGHT POLLUTION
noaa_source: NASA VIIRS Black Marble annual nighttime-lights composite via NASA GIBS (Román et al., Suomi NPP VIIRS Day/Night Band)
product_name: NASA VIIRS Black Marble annual nighttime-lights composite via NASA GIBS (Román et al., Suomi NPP VIIRS Day/Night Band)
variable: Annual artificial nighttime brightness distribution (VIIRS DNB composite visualization, relative brightness index)
units: relative brightness index 0-100 (display; tile-background floor subtraction + skyglow bloom + square-root stretch of the published composite visualization; monotonic, ordering preserved)
spatial_resolution_source: NASA GIBS 500m WMTS tiles (level 6, 4.5-degree) mosaicked to the common canvas
spatial_resolution_rendered: 1800x1175 canvas over lon [-93.0,-73.5], lat [40.5,49.5] (mean-value binning, no upsampling of source precision)
missing_data_treatment: tile-background floor subtraction, NaN-aware skyglow bloom (radius 10 x 3 passes), then square-root 100*sqrt(bloomed/ref) mapping against the 99.99th percentile (monotonic perceptual mapping so metro glow reads at basin scale); full basin rectangle, no shoreline cut; untiled canvas pixels transparent; never zero-filled.
shoreline_mask: assets/great_lakes_watermask.png — shared NOAA medium-resolution shoreline water mask (nautical-chart compilation, mean-high-water datum; snapped + polygonized once, full vertex precision, antialiased). Overlay alpha is multiplied by this mask and edge RGB is bled into transparent pixels (anti-fringe for bilinear clients), so every product shares one shoreline.

legend_scale_html: Artificial night-sky brightness on the Bortle dark-sky scale Classes 1–9 (John E. Bortle, Sky & Telescope 2001; keyed from the NASA VIIRS Black Marble annual composite): LOWEST Class 1 Excellent dark-sky site near-black (NELM 7.6–8.0) → Class 2 True dark slate-gray → Class 3 Rural blue → Class 4 Rural/suburban teal-green → Class 5 Suburban olive → Class 6 Bright suburban gold → Class 7 Suburban/urban orange → Class 8 City-sky red → HIGHEST+ Class 9 Inner-city sky near-white (NELM ≤4.0). Classes 1–5 use widely separated hues so dark skies stay readable. Class boundaries are log-spaced on the brightness index (3.2 / 7.4 / 12.8 / 19.8 / 28.8 / 40.5 / 55.5 / 74.9), shaped like the published SQM retrofit table — an approximate relative classification from composite imagery, not a calibrated SQM measurement. Same sky always shows the same class.
bortle_methodology: Approximate relative Bortle classification. Class titles and NELM are Bortle's own (Sky & Telescope, Feb 2001); SQM ranges are the widely-circulated third-party retrofit approximations (Bortle's original contains no SQM values). Index breakpoints are log-spaced (100*(10^(k/9)-1)/9), shaped like the published SQM retrofit table, because night-light brightness is log-distributed. NOT a calibrated SQM measurement; the input is GIBS composite-imagery luminance, not nW/cm2/sr radiance.
folder_html:
LIVE LIGHT POLLUTION

Environmental artificial night-sky brightness around the Great Lakes from NASA's VIIRS Black Marble annual composite: a continuous surface showing where city glow and development illuminate the night most strongly and where genuinely dark skies remain. Bright cores mark metropolitan light domes; dark blues mark the darkest shorelines and waters.

Light-pollution science (a branch of environmental photometry and ecology) studies artificial skyglow from electric lighting: it disrupts circadian rhythms in wildlife and humans, wastes energy, and erases natural starlight. Satellite day/night-band radiometry separates artificial glow from natural night-sky brightness (moonlight, airglow, starlight), mapping an environmental pressure distinct from any single observatory or preserve boundary.
